chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who said:

I sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) some dirhams, for me and for others, and I wrote to him informing him that they are from the Fitra of the dependents. So he wrote in his own handwriting: 'I have taken possession of it, and accepted'.

key_terms.الدَّرَاهِم: Dirhams, silver coins used as currency
key_terms.الْعِيَال: Dependents, family members for whom one provides support
key_terms.فِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory alms given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam accept Zakat al-Fitr payments from his followers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s acceptance of monetary payment for Zakat al-Fitr on behalf of dependents, a key basis for the Shia juristic view that dirhams can substitute for food items. The Imam’s personal handwriting ('qabidtu wa qabiltu') serves as a direct authentication of the transaction, reinforcing the authority of the Imam in collecting and distributing alms. This practice underscores the communal responsibility of providing for the poor during Eid, linking individual piety with social welfare.
